title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is working with a basic localizer W in (Cat), the induced class W_A = i_A^{-1}(W) of weak equivalences in the presheaf category Â, and the localizations Hot_A = W_A^{-1}Â and Hot(W) = W^{-1}(Cat). On the previous page he asks whether Hot_A admits a calculus of fractions, specifically a cancellation (Ore-type) property: given s in W_A with fs = gs, is there t in W_A with tf = tg? He answers it with a cylinder argument. The cylinder is built from the pushout M of I×X' and X⊔X along X'⊔X'. That argument rests on cofibration-category-type axioms on a class 𝓜 of arrows: (i) every map factors as an 𝓜-map followed by a homotopism; (ii) cobase change of a weak equivalence along an 𝓜-map stays a weak equivalence (left properness); (iii) there are generating intervals I_α with X⊔X → X×I_α in 𝓜, which he calls 'separating intervals'; (iv) sums of weak equivalences are weak equivalences.

This page does the bookkeeping for that argument.

First, the argument needed a separating interval, meaning δ0, δ1 : e → I are disjoint, so that X⊔X → X×I is a monomorphism. For M = Â one therefore needs a separating interval I in Â that also defines a homotopy structure on Â compatible with W_A. He says this holds iff I → e is W_A-aspherical, i.e. a×I → a lies in W_A for every object a of A. He also notes a variant: δ0 and δ1 have the same image in the localization. He concludes this is exactly the condition that A be a local test category. This is his known criterion: A is a local test category iff Â has a separating, locally aspherical interval (equivalently, the Lawvere interval is locally aspherical).

Second, the argument also used that sums of W_A-maps are in W_A; only the case card I = 2 was needed. Since i_A commutes with sums, this reduces to (Cat) and W. There it follows from axiom Loc 3, the localization/fibrewise axiom. Take J to be the discrete category on the index set, and view ∐f_i : ∐X_i → ∐Y_i as a map over J. The induced maps on the slices over each j are just the f_i, which lie in W, so the total map is in W. A 'Coroll…' is begun and struck; the next page states Corollary 1: finite sums exist in Hot(W), and the canonical functors (Cat) → Hot(W) and Â → Hot_A → Hot(W) commute with them.
errors: No mathematical error. The reasoning is sketchy: the 'iff' between compatibility of the interval homotopy with W and W_A-asphericity of I → e is asserted, not proved.

The bracketed variant (δ0, δ1 having equal images in the localization) is in general only a global condition. As stated it is weaker than local asphericity unless it is imposed locally, over each a in A.
Loc 3 with a discrete J gives arbitrary, not just finite, sums. The restriction to card I = 2 is unnecessary, which a marginal note on the next page also acknowledges.

ideas.what: Characterization of local test categories by existence of a separating interval I in Â with I → e W_A-aspherical (locally aspherical)
ideas.modern_name: Criterion for local test categories (separating locally aspherical interval / Lawvere interval)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks); systematized by Maltsiniotis (Astérisque 301, 2005) and Cisinski (Astérisque 308, 2006)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (sections on test categories and local test categories)

ideas.what: Cofibration-category-style axioms (factorization, left properness, cylinder via separating interval, sums) used to obtain a calculus of fractions in Hot_A
ideas.modern_name: Left proper cofibration category / Cisinski model structure on presheaves with monomorphisms as cofibrations
ideas.usually_credited_to: K.S. Brown (1973), Quillen (1967); Cisinski (2002–2006) for presheaf categories over local test categories
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses 'homotopy interval' structures and asphericity; this precise axiom list is not known to be published

ideas.what: Sums of weak equivalences are weak equivalences, deduced from the localization axiom Loc 3 over a discrete base category
ideas.modern_name: Stability of a basic localizer under (co)products

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up the cylinder/calculus-of-fractions argument for W_A on Â. It recovers the known characterization of local test categories via separating locally aspherical intervals and a routine consequence of Loc 3. All of this is consistent with Pursuing Stacks and with the later work of Maltsiniotis and Cisinski, which went further (model structures). Nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The struck word at the bottom ('[-Gevolt[?]-]') is most likely 'Coroll[aire]', begun and then struck. The next page opens with 'Corollaire 1'.
Line 1: the word inserted above 'utiliser' plausibly reads 'moralement' rather than 'montrer'.
Line 1: '(cf condition iii)' is written as '(cf condition (iii))'.
'qui de plus définisse une {+[?]+} ... homotopie pour Â' is better read as 'qui de plus définisse une [structure?] homotopique pour Â ... compatible avec W' ('homotopiques' is visible).
The bracket reads approximately '[ou des deux sections δ0 et δ1 : e → I aient même image dans W...]'. It refers to δ0, δ1 having equal images, not to a struck 'les deux'.
The final diagram is a triangle X → Y over J (X → J, Y → J), with J the discrete index category. The transcription's '[?]' there can be resolved this way.
'pour card I = 2' should read 'pour card I = 2' with I the index set of the family, not the interval I.
